L01.why: Expletive 'there was' cannot name a doer and so is least likely to fix a dangling modifier, but it is grammatical.

L02.why: Comma-bounded 'by then' between two clauses risks a comma splice, though a dependent opener could rescue it.

L03.why: Plural active progressive fits some subject; none impossible.

L04.why: A noun phrase may not fit the slot, but 'requires careful anticipation' is possible.

L05.why: An infinitive of purpose with a 2000-year time phrase is awkward, but not impossible.

L06.why: A comma between subject and verb is usually wrong, but closes a nonrestrictive modifier in some sentences.

L08.why: Bare noun 'collaboration' may not fit the slot, though some frames allow it.

L09.why: 'nurses's' is never a standard possessive form of 'nurses'.

L10.why: 'however' needs boundary punctuation it may lack, but some frames make it fine.

L11.why: Impersonal 'it was found' cannot supply a doer for an opening modifier, but is grammatical.

L12.why: 'hospital, turn' risks a comma splice or bare verb, but a series could fit.

L13.why: Each verb form fits some subject and tense.

L14.why: 'consequently but' is almost never idiomatic, though a contrastive frame could conceivably use it.

L15.why: 'entrance, its' risks a comma splice, but an absolute phrase can make it correct.

L16.why: 'would had' is never grammatical; a modal takes a bare verb.

L17.why: No punctuation before 'a' may run elements together, but some frames need none.

L18.why: Without the chef as subject a dangling modifier is likely, but the hidden opener is unknown.

L19.why: A participle alone may leave no main verb, but some frames allow it.

L20.why: Run-on risk with no punctuation, though some frames need none.

L21.why: A semicolon before a dependent 'although' clause is usually wrong, but the clause might be independent.

L22.why: Missing comma after an introductory element is likely wrong, but the frame is hidden.

L23.why: Active plural progressive fits some subject.

L24.why: 'keep' changes meaning but fits some frame.

L25.why: 'being less intuitive' may fit some frame.

L26.why: An infinitive of purpose is the odd modifier out, but grammatical.

L27.why: An unclosed parenthetical comma is usually wrong, unless the phrase ends the sentence.

L28.why: Subject pronoun 'he' after a preposition or as object is usually wrong, but 'than he' frames exist.

L29.why: ' that is' without punctuation is unusual, but possible.

L30.why: A closing parenthesis needs an opener that may not exist, but one might.

L31.why: A nominalized possessive subject is awkward but grammatical.

L32.why: Comma-bounded 'however' between clauses risks a splice, but may be mid-clause.

L33.why: Plural 'come' after a comma depends on the subject; possible.

L34.why: Laid/lain choice depends on transitivity, unknown without the sentence.

L35.why: Infinitive may not fit, but possible.

L36.why: Infinitive may not fit, but possible.

L38.why: 'pane, consequently,' risks a comma splice, but possible in some frames.
